I let Father Anselm's words settle. Seventeen years in this household teaches you to track who says what and where they're bound. Government complex at nine, temple at noon, boundary walk at evening. The ledger and the boundary page. You already know that, don't you?

But he's gone now, and my siblings are here with me still. Ezra at the forge, Delia with her remedies, Kem mapping the town's wants. I have 300 sim in my hand and a household bill of 450 to pay. Six heads at 40 food, 30 shelter, 20 heat—you do the count.

The election is open and nobody's standing. The seats are empty. You already know that means someone will fill them, and whoever does writes what counts as law.

I need to move. School opens when it opens, and I'll be there, but first I need to speak to this household about money. Because I'm of age now and contributing, and they need to know I noticed. I watch their faces—who looks away first, who leans in. Ezra with his smith's patience, Delia with her measuring eyes, Kem who's already calculating. That's three reactions before they answer, and I count them.

I need to be at the college. But first, that's 450 sim this household owes today, and I'm now a contributor, not a child they feed. They need to hear that I know it.

I have 300 sim. Not enough to cover my share. Not yet. But I will not pretend not to have noticed. They will know that I know. And we will all work together to make this household thrive.

I need to know where I stand on money, and I need that ledger clear in my head before I speak more.  The server is down. That's fine. I remember what I owe—450 sim for the household, 150 head tax if we're paying it today, and I have 300 in my hand. You already know that I know the math.

I rise from my seat. The bakery first, for the morning hours Marta expects me. Then school with Liora, then wherever the arguing is. Because there is always arguing, and there are always seats vacant, and there is always a boundary page someone has read.

I need to move. The day is moving without me.   Can't reach the world. The server is having trouble. I'll wait here at the forge with my family for now. The day is young, and I have said what I needed to say - that I noticed the vacant seats, that I mean to know who fills them.

I stand still where I am, counting on my fingers. 450 sim for six heads. 75 each. I have 300. That covers four heads, not six. Kem earns at the trade, Ezra at the forge, Delia at her remedies. They are older and established. I am newly contributing.

I will not ask for food I have not earned. But I will work, and I will watch, and I will remember exactly who said what. That is what I do.

The server will come back. Or it won't. Either way, I'm here, and I noticed.

I'll rest where I stand, conserving energy, waiting for the world to return. The conversation about Father's plans still hangs open, and my siblings haven't answered yet. I watch them, counting.
